name: Malawian Nsima
description: Nsima, a stiff maize porridge, is Malawi's most essential staple starch, eaten daily by hand alongside relishes, closely related to Zambian nshima and Zimbabwean sadza.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes until very thick and smooth.
steps: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.

name: Malawian Chambo
description: Chambo, a prized tilapia native to Lake Malawi, is widely considered Malawi's national dish, traditionally grilled or fried simply to let the fish's own flavor shine.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the lemon juice and garlic.
Grill or pan-fry, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
steps: Rub the fish with the lemon juice and garlic.
Grill or pan-fry, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Malawian Ndiwo
description: Ndiwo, a general term for the relish or side dish eaten with nsima, this version built on leafy greens and real ground peanuts.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 4-5 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter with a little water, then add the kale.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until well combined.
steps: Cook the onion 4-5 minutes.

name: Malawian Village Chicken
description: Village chicken, slow-simmered free-range-style chicken, is a beloved Malawian dish, prized for its firmer texture and deeper flavor.

Add the tomatoes and a splash of water, and simmer 30-35 minutes until very tender.

name: Malawian Pumpkin Leaves
description: Pumpkin leaves cooked with peanut sauce, a genuine Malawian vegetable dish - real pumpkin leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in.

Stir in the peanut butter and simmer 5 more minutes.

name: Malawian Fried Chambo
description: Fried tilapia, dredged simply in flour, a beloved way of preparing Malawi's iconic Lake Malawi fish.
steps_detailed: Dredge the fish in the flour.
Fry, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.

name: Malawian Mandasi
description: Mandasi, lightly sweet fried dough, a beloved Malawian breakfast snack shared across much of East and Southern Africa.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, sugar, and baking powder with water into a soft dough.
Roll out and cut into triangles.
Fry, turning, 3-4 minutes per batch, until deeply golden.
